Platinum-based chemoimmunotherapy achieves maximal tumor response in the induction phase but carries substantial toxicity. Thus, most novel ICI combinations are increasingly investigated in the maintenance setting 38–40. Our sequential design was rationally constructed to avoid additive toxicity from concurrent chemo-immunoradiotherapy and minimize target volumes by delivering focal radiotherapy in the setting of reduced tumor burden. This optimized treatment sequence appears to account for both the promising survival efficacy and the favorable safety outcomes. Compared with Gray et al. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) comprises heterogeneous pathological subtypes and molecular profiles . From a molecular and therapeutic perspective, NSCLC can be broadly categorized into 2 groups: driver gene-positive and driver gene-negative. While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have provided substantial clinical benefit to patients with driver gene-negative tumors, a substantial proportion of those with advanced disease still do not achieve long-term survival 1–3. Therefore, overcoming immune resistance remains a major therapeutic challenge.
